name: Results — did you find what you needed?
description: Asks at the moment of truth, right after a menu loads. The feedback button and the day-7 NPS both miss this moment, and passive feedback buttons get responses from well under 1% of users.

questions.question: Did you find what you needed?
What was missing?
questions.description: Optional — a dish, a whole menu, or something else.

_notes: 15s delay so it lands after they have actually read some dishes, not while the page is still settling.

name: City guide — was this useful?
description: The guides are a separate job from the search box (browse vs. look up a specific place) and deserve their own signal.

questions.question: What would make it more useful?

_notes: URL-targeted rather than event-targeted: guide pages have a stable, identifiable path.

name: Failure — what were you looking for?
description: The highest-value survey of the three: it catches people at the exact moment the product let them down, and tells us what they wanted in their own words. Answers what no funnel chart can.

questions.question: Sorry — what were you hoping to find?
questions.description: Tell us the restaurant or dish you were after and we will take a look by hand.

appearance.thankYouMessageHeader: Thanks — we will look into it.

_notes: Event-triggered, NOT URL-targeted, and that is deliberate: the search error state lives inside HeroSearch on '/', while a no-menu result renders at /restaurant/[id]. There is no URL that means 'something went wrong', so targeting by URL would either miss the error case or fire on healthy pages.
